title: Closures in Structs
goal: Learn how to store a closure in a struct field and call it.

sections.text: Every closure in Rust has a unique type generated by the compiler. To store a closure in a struct, you use a generic parameter bound by a closure trait.

sections.caption: The struct is generic over the unnamable closure type F.

sections.text: When calling a closure stored in a field, wrap the field access in parentheses. Without parentheses, Rust looks for a method with that name instead of calling the closure.

sections.caption: Parentheses disambiguate field calls from method calls.

sections.text: Writing `self.predicate(val)` produces compiler error `E0599` because Rust searches for a method named `predicate` on `Filter`.

explanation: Learn how to store a closure in a struct field and call it.
